p4.lm-head-fran-vektor-till.1: LM head: from vector to logits
p4.lm-head-fran-vektor-till.3: W_U (unembedding, lm_head) gives one number per token in the vocabulary and per position. The logit at position t is the model’s estimate of what comes at position t + 1.
p4.lm-head-fran-vektor-till.4: During generation only the last row is needed. vLLM therefore computes logits only for the last position of each sequence. Computing all T rows for a long prompt would waste T × 128,256 numbers.
p4.lm-head-fran-vektor-till.5: In some models the LM head shares weights with the embedding table (tied embeddings). Llama-3-8B does not.
p4.lm-head-fran-vektor-till.9: one number per possible next token
p4.lm-head-fran-vektor-till.10: Only the last row (dark) is computed during generation. The diagram is not to scale.
p4.sampling-temperature-top-k.2:
p = softmax(logits / temperature)
top-k: keep the k largest
top-p: keep the smallest set with Σp ≥ top_p
renormalize, draw one token
p4.sampling-temperature-top-k.3: Temperature < 1 sharpens the distribution, > 1 flattens it. Temperature 0 means greedy: always take the largest.
p4.sampling-temperature-top-k.4: Top-k cuts away everything but the k best.
p4.sampling-temperature-top-k.5: Top-p (nucleus) cuts adaptively: few candidates remain when the model is confident, many when it is unsure.
p4.sampling-temperature-top-k.6: The logits after “Katten satt på” below are made up, but the mechanics are exactly what runs.
p4.den-autoregressiva-loopen.2: A generated token is appended to the sequence and the whole model runs again. The response grows by one token per pass until one of these happens:
p4.den-autoregressiva-loopen.3: the model produces a stop token (<|eot_id|>)
p4.den-autoregressiva-loopen.4: a stop string matches the detokenized text
p4.den-autoregressiva-loopen.5: max_tokens for the request is reached
p4.den-autoregressiva-loopen.6: the sequence reaches the model’s max_model_len
p4.den-autoregressiva-loopen.7: Without a KV cache, every pass would recompute the whole sequence. With the cache, only the new position is computed, but every pass still has to read all the weights. That is the basis for everything in module 6.
p4.den-autoregressiva-loopen.8: Greedy (temperature 0) is not guaranteed to be deterministic on a server. Different batch sizes can order floating-point operations differently, and small differences can flip a close argmax.
p4.testa-dig-sjalv-logits.2: How big is the logits tensor if you (incorrectly) compute logits for every position in an 8,000-token prompt, in fp32?
p4.testa-dig-sjalv-logits.3: 8,000 × 128,256 × 4 bytes ≈ 4.1 GB. That is why only the last position is computed.
p4.testa-dig-sjalv-logits.4: What does top-p = 0.9 do when the model gives 95% to a single token?
p4.testa-dig-sjalv-logits.5: Only that token remains, because it alone reaches 0.9. Sampling then effectively becomes greedy.
p4.testa-dig-sjalv-logits.6: Why can temperature 0 give different answers to the same question on a server with many users?
p4.testa-dig-sjalv-logits.7: Batch composition affects kernel selection and summation order. Floating-point addition is not associative, so logits can differ in the last decimal place and flip a close argmax.
p4.traning-next-token-loss.2: During training the target for each position is simply the next token in the text. Inputs and targets are the same sequence, shifted one step.
p4.traning-next-token-loss.3:
logits  = model(ids)            [B, T, V]
targets = ids shifted one step  [B, T]
loss    = −mean log softmax(logits)[target]
p4.traning-next-token-loss.4: Thanks to the causal mask, all T predictions are computed in a single forward pass. That is why training is parallel across the sequence while generation is serial: at generation time the next token does not exist until it has been sampled.
p4.traning-next-token-loss.7: The position that sees “Katten satt på” is trained to give high probability to “ mattan”.
p4.gradienter-och-minne.2: Backpropagation produces a gradient with exactly the same shape as each weight matrix. The optimizer (AdamW) updates the weights in the direction opposite to the gradient and keeps two states of its own per parameter.
p4.gradienter-och-minne.3: With mixed precision each parameter costs about 16 bytes during training, versus 2 bytes at inference. On top of that come the activations that must be stored for the backward pass.
p4.gradienter-och-minne.4: That is why you can run an 8B model on a 24 GB GPU, while full fine-tuning of the same model fits on a single node with eight GPUs. With LoRA or QLoRA, one GPU is enough. It is pretraining from scratch that requires a cluster, and there it is at least as much about compute and time as about memory.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.2: The architecture is the same across all phases. Only the weights change, and with them the behavior.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.4: Trillions of tokens of web text, code, books.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.5: Goal: the next token. Learns language and facts.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.6: Result: a base model that continues text.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.8: Example dialogues in the chat template.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.9: The same loss, but only on the assistant’s answer.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.10: Learns the format, the roles and the stop token.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.14: gives reasoning models with long thinking.
p4.fran-basmodell-till.15: For inference the phase is irrelevant: a reasoning model runs exactly like an ordinary one. It just generates far more tokens before the answer, which shows up in cost and latency.
